narrative:
The model estimates a 48% chance that you will leave your current role, which is high enough for the organization to deny your promotion as a precaution.

Three factors stood out most in the decision. First, having received other job opportunities while at the company pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving. Employees who stay rarely report outside offers, so this signal carried significant weight. Second, your six to ten years in your current role worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward staying; most employees predicted to remain have shorter tenure in their last organization. Third, your overall career experience of six to ten years also nudged the outcome slightly toward leaving, though less forcefully than the other two factors.

Taken together, the model sees your external opportunities as the dominant reason it expects you might depart, despite your solid tenure and experience. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether additional internal growth opportunities could reduce the pull of outside offers. You, in turn, may want to reflect on what would make staying feel more rewarding before making any decisions.
